title: Ocean Giants
blurb: Put a swimmer, a great white, an orca, a whale shark, a sperm whale and a blue whale at the same scale and the last row stops being a statistic. The sea grows animals a size the land has never managed to support.

title: The Largest Animal Ever
sub: Bigger than any dinosaur, and still here
blurb: A blue whale runs to 30 metres and 150 tonnes — heavier than any dinosaur ever found. Its heart is the size of a small car and beats about eight times a minute while it dives.

title: Where the Light Ends
sub: Sunlight runs out long before the water does
blurb: Only about one per cent of surface light reaches 200 metres, which is the last depth at which a plant can make a living. By 1,000 metres there is no sunlight at all — and the ocean averages 3,682 metres deep.

title: Why the Sea Is Blue
sub: Blue is what is left over
blurb: Water absorbs the long wavelengths first. Red is effectively gone within five metres, orange by twenty, yellow by forty, green by eighty. Blue is simply the colour that survives longest, which is why everything down there looks like it.

title: Half the Air You Breathe
sub: Every second breath came from the sea
blurb: Phytoplankton are drifting plants too small to see, and together they produce roughly half of the oxygen in the atmosphere. They out-produce every forest on land, and a single drop of seawater can hold thousands of them.

title: Waves Move, Water Does Not
sub: What crosses the ocean is energy
blurb: A float on a passing wave traces a circle and ends up where it started. The crest travels; the water only goes round. A Pacific swell can cross 10,000 kilometres while the sea it passes through barely moves at all.
